characteristics.cultivar: Taiwanese oolong cultivars (Jin Xuan, Cui Yu) introduced by Taiwanese investors

description.short: Taiwanese-style oolongs from basalt plateaus, floral and creamy, cultivated primarily for export
description.overview: Since the 1990s, the region was heavily developed by Taiwanese tea producers who transplanted classic cultivars and crafting techniques to Vietnam's mineral-rich basalt soils.
description.aroma: Creamy, floral, echoing high-mountain Taiwanese oolongs
description.taste: Smooth, velvety, floral with mild natural sweetness
description.processing: Classic Taiwanese light oolong crafting: withering → tumbling → kill-green → ball rolling → gentle drying

history.origin: The Central Highlands of Vietnam were historically world-famous for Robusta coffee, but starting in the 1990s, Taiwanese entrepreneurs established high-grade oolong plantations in Bao Loc.
history.development: The fertile volcanic soil and elevation proved exceptionally well-suited for cultivars like Jin Xuan and Four Seasons Spring, achieving quality that rivals domestic Taiwanese teas.
history.modern: A large portion of Lam Dong oolong is exported directly to Taiwan and regional Asian markets, valued for its quality-to-price ratio.
interestingFacts: Lam Dong is an example of complete cross-border transfer of tea cultivars, machinery, and master processing techniques from Taiwan to mainland Southeast Asia.
Bao Loc is uniquely positioned as both a premier center for high-grade oolong and one of the world's highest-volume Robusta coffee producing regions.
